reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic pattern with a fundamental period of ~18 points, consistent across all candidates. Normal behavior features sharp, V- or U-shaped troughs (depths typically −0.2 to −0.3 in robust standardized units) followed by asymmetric recoveries: rapid rise (1–3 points) then slower plateau or gentle slope. Peaks are broad and relatively flat-topped, often sustaining for 2–4 points near +1.2 to +1.5, with occasional minor secondary humps. Amplitude (90th percentile range) varies from ~1.5 to 3.0 due to scaling with window length, but normalized peak-to-trough excursion is consistently ~1.4–1.7. Noise is low: most segments show minimal high-frequency jitter; roughness values <0.7 indicate smooth transitions except where intentional step-like plateaus occur. Baseline level drifts slightly across long windows (e.g., candidate 3 shows mild upward trend over 5 cycles), but local trends per cycle are near-zero (slope_per_point ∈ [−0.033, +0.005]). Truncation at boundaries is acceptable when the motif is完整 within the window (e.g., full trough–peak pair visible). Acceptable variation includes: (i) occasional flattened peaks (plateaus), (ii) minor step changes in baseline between cycles, (iii) slight asymmetry in trough recovery speed. Anomalies would manifest as abnormally deep/sharp troughs (>−0.5), sustained flatlines >6 points, missing expected troughs, or abrupt non-periodic spikes.

reference_profiles.description: One clean period (18 pts): highly regular sawtooth-like cycle with deep symmetric troughs (~0.12), sharp rises, and flat-topped peaks (~1.5). Very low roughness (0.54), minimal noise, no trend. Ideal morphology for single-cycle matching.

Three periods (54 pts): shows repeated trough-peak motifs but with more variability—some troughs shallower, some peaks less flat; includes brief plateaus and a mild positive slope. Higher amplitude (2.34) and lower roughness (0.13) suggest smoother transitions; contains one unusually high peak (~1.96) possibly due to mild contamination or natural variation.

Three periods (54 pts): similar motif structure to candidate 1 but with stronger negative slope (−0.033), deeper troughs on average, and higher roughness (0.67). Peaks remain broad but less flat; more jagged transitions suggest slightly higher noise or micro-variability. No obvious outliers; consensus-compatible despite higher variability.

Five periods (90 pts): longest window; reveals slow upward baseline drift and one prominent high-amplitude transient (~2.6) around point 2788, likely a benign system-level shift rather than anomaly (matches periodicity). Otherwise preserves core motif: regular troughs, broad peaks, and step-like plateaus. Highest amplitude (3.04) reflects cumulative scale, not abnormality.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries of length ~18 (1-cycle) due to its purity and symmetry. For 3-cycle queries (~54 pts), use reference 2 as primary (higher reliability, negative trend matches common behavior); fallback to reference 1 if query shows mild positive drift. For 5-cycle or longer queries, reference 3 is best despite its drift—it captures long-horizon stability and acceptable transients. When query shows unusually deep troughs (<−0.4) or flatlines >5 pts, none of the references support that as normal; flag as anomalous.
